reviewer: Claude Opus 5, WP3-C settings lane (evidence run executed in this session)
reviewedChange: The page stopped resolving its Project with getActiveWorkspace(), whose third fallback returns LEGACY_WORKSPACE_ID - a real workspace holding real tasks for which the caller has produced no membership proof (D-005) - so a caller belonging to nothing could be shown a stranger's member roster and Danger Zone. It now calls requireRouteProjectId(), which stops at the first-membership fallback and redirects to /welcome instead. It accepts no explicit workspaceId on purpose: this surface renders inside the shared app chrome, so accepting one would let the URL and the chrome name different Projects. getMyRoleInActiveWorkspace, which gates every owner-only section, resolved a Project of its own accord; it becomes getMyRoleInProject(ws, me), so the role that gates the page and the Project the page renders are the same one, and it folds into the existing Promise.all so the page makes one fewer round-trip level than before. The four panels then pass the id they were rendered from into every mutation, which is the half a capability proof cannot do alone: the Danger Zone asks the operator to type the name of the Project it is about to destroy, and that name came from this render, so a cookie that moved between render and click would have named one Project and deleted another. The rendered surface is safe because none of this runs for the review fixture - the isDemoMode() branch returns before the first line that changed, and it is untouched - and because for an authorized caller the resolved Project is identical to what the accessor returned, so layout, copy and DOM of all nine sections are unchanged. The one operator-visible behaviour change is that a co-owner now receives an honest refusal from the delete control instead of destroying a Project that capabilities.ts reserves to the primary owner. This entry has no direct fixture case (fixtureCoverage: none), so the evidence bound here is the suite-wide run of 132 browser tests across four breakpoints that passed after the change, plus screenshots captured from that same build.
